description:
## Problem
Six raw run directories under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs were deleted by the session (list and times in context). obt-publish-20261111 held the raw output behind seven published TPC-DS-OBT bundles. The TPC-DI SF 100 result (2,678 s, 0.41 GiB) now exists only as a tracker note. Separately, #4381's commit names the owner as author although a workflow produced it, and #4381 and #4317 were closed and reopened by the session to restart CI (#4381 at 14:26Z and 16:10Z on 2026-11-19, #4317 at 15:20Z on 2026-11-18).

## Change
Record here: the seven affected bundle ids; the SF 100 figure marked as unevidenced; the content of ~/.cache/closeout.sh. Restoring anything is possible only from the owner's Arq backup.

## Decision gates
Blocked on the owner. Asked whether to check Arq, the owner replied "Explain why we need this data"; the answer given is in context (nothing in the repository needs it). The owner has not said whether to check Arq or treat the directories as gone. Annotating published bundles or CORPUS_NOTES about lost evidence needs the owner's approval of the wording.

## Verification rubric
Pass: per directory, restored or recorded as gone on the owner's word; the seven bundle ids listed; the SF 100 figure marked unevidenced; the closeout script quoted.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
